content:
I've been using the iPhone 18 Pro for the past week, after spending a full year with the iPhone Air. While both phones have their strengths, my main takeaway from the iPhone 18 Pro is this: absolutely zero compromises. Allow me to explain.

iPhone 18 Pro: The best camera system, battery life, and performance

If you're in the market for a new iPhone, the iPhone 18 Pro is almost certainly one of the top contenders.

My unit, which I've been using for a week now, is the burgundy colorway, and it replaced my iPhone Air. Although I loved the Air, matching what Apple has done with the "zero compromises" approach on the iPhone 18 Pro is no easy feat.

  • The cameras on the iPhone 18 Pro are better than the Air's, and they're more versatile. The telephoto and ultrawide lenses come in handy for specific scenarios, but even the main lens on the iPhone 18 Pro is noticeably superior.
  • Battery life is equally satisfying. With the iPhone Air, I felt like the battery was generally adequate for a day, sometimes requiring a top-up in the afternoon. After switching to the iPhone 18 Pro, I don't even have to think about "is my battery about to die" anymore.
  • Performance is top-notch as well. The A20 Pro chip makes everything on the iPhone run incredibly fast, and I've also noticed that Siri AI feels more responsive. Combined with the vapor chamber helping with thermal management, I've encountered zero overheating issues—something the Air occasionally suffered from.

I'm not a professional photographer, and if you're looking for battery tests or performance benchmarks, my colleague Chance's iPhone 18 Pro review has everything you need. But after spending a week with the iPhone 18 Pro, the word "best" keeps popping into my mind.

The iPhone 18 Pro (and Pro Max) features Apple's most premium camera system to date, offers the best battery life, and outperforms other models in terms of performance. I've also noticed some more subtle improvements: the enhanced built-in speaker quality and the upgraded Dynamic Island are highlights.

All of the above are quantifiable gaps, but what I appreciate even more is the peace of mind that comes from knowing my iPhone offers Apple's "best" in every critical aspect. No more worrying: Would the photos of my family look better if taken with a different iPhone? Would that lag not have happened?

Setting aside all the merits of the iPhone 18 Pro, I must admit I'm still incredibly excited about the upcoming iPhone Duo.

iPhone Duo and iPhone Air: Similar in that they involve trade-offs, but incredibly appealing

The iPhone Air and iPhone Duo share a lot of similarities. Beyond their similar design language, both come with shortcomings.

Just like my iPhone Air, the iPhone Duo's camera system will be weaker than the iPhone 18 Pro's. The battery might be comparable, but certainly not as good as the Pro Max, and I suspect sustained performance will also fall slightly behind. The iPhone Duo will also lack Face ID and the Action button.

However, despite these trade-offs, I'm still very much looking forward to trying the phone out for myself.

Because it brings many innovations that the iPhone 18 Pro doesn't have. The foldable form factor design can be considered one of the biggest hardware changes in iPhone history.

I've thoroughly enjoyed my time with the iPhone 18 Pro this week. But guess what happened yesterday when I picked up my iPhone Air again?

I immediately said: "Wow."

After a year with the Air's slim profile, I had taken it for granted. But after a few days with the iPhone 18 Pro, picking up the Air made me rediscover just how futuristic that phone feels. I expect the iPhone Duo will evoke a similar feeling—not just in terms of design, but also in its practicality.

I can't wait to pocket an iPad-like experience. Although I must admit I have mixed feelings about the shortcomings the Duo brings, the anticipation is still very real.

The days of Apple offering just one "best" iPhone are long gone. If you want a zero-compromise device, both the iPhone 18 Pro and Pro Max appear to be excellent choices. But if you're looking for something more futuristic and unique, I still can't wait to try the iPhone Duo.

How do you choose between the iPhone 18 Pro and the iPhone Duo? Let us know in the comments.
